paraphrase: To think that practice and realization are not one is a non-Buddhist view; in the buddha-dharma practice and realization are one (shushō ittō); because practice is practice-in-realization, the beginner's wholehearted practice is the whole of original realization; teachers therefore say not to look for realization apart from practice.
speaker: Dōgen

paraphrase: Rejects the view that the mind-nature is permanent while the body perishes, so that on death the nature leaves the body and returns to the ocean of nature: this is the view of the heretic Śreṇika; in the buddha-dharma body and mind are one, nature and form are not two.
